speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have significant symptoms including fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To better understand your condition, have these symptoms been present for more than a few weeks, and have you noticed any night sweats severe enough to soak your bedding?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).
REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests and LDH levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC): WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): Not Available. Liver Function Tests: Not Available. LDH levels: Elevated.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the elevated LDH and white blood cell count alongside your "B symptoms" (night sweats, weight loss), this strongly suggests a lymphoproliferative disorder. Have you experienced any unexplained fevers, or any changes in your skin such as itching or a rash? Also, have you noticed any pain in your bones or joints?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming the timeline and severity of your "B symptoms." Given the elevated LDH, weight loss, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, I need to determine if there is a specific infection or malignancy involved. Have you had any recent contact with a tuberculosis patient, or do you notice any cough, shortness of breath, or skin lesions? Additionally, have you noticed any night sweats severe enough to soak your bedding, and have you experienced any bone pain or joint swelling?

REQUEST TEST: Tuberculosis (TB) Quantiferon Gold Test.
REQUEST TEST: HIV Antibody/Antigen Test.
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest X-Ray.

text: RESULTS: Tuberculosis (TB) Quantiferon Gold Test: Not Available. HIV Antibody/Antigen Test: Not Available. Chest X-Ray: Not Available.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the lack of infectious markers so far and your history of supraclavicular lymphadenopathy with elevated LDH and night sweats, have you noticed any pain in the testicles or any new lumps under your arms or in your neck? Additionally, do you have a family history of lymphoma or leukemia?

REQUEST TEST: LDH level confirmation and repeat CBC.
REQUEST IMAGES: CT Scan of the Neck, Chest, and Abdomen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: LDH level confirmation: Elevated. Repeat CBC: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. CT Scan of the Neck, Chest, and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (Highly suggestive of Hodgkin Lymphoma given supraclavicular mass, B-symptoms, elevated LDH, and mediastinal involvement).
